content.value_statement: Choosing among many Groove commands can interrupt engineering work. This skill maps natural-language requests to the best workflow and preserves important details.
actual_capabilities: Routes a natural-language request to one best-matching Groove skill.
Displays the grouped Groove command catalog when no request is provided.
Passes residual scope and details to the selected workflow.
Offers two to four choices when several workflows match.
Requests confirmation before sensitive administration or publishing workflows.
Enables Groovebook routes only when Groovebook is configured.
limitations: Requires the related Groove workflow skills to be installed and available.
Routes requests but does not implement downstream workflows itself.
Selects one workflow per request instead of coordinating multiple workflows.
Reads project Groove configuration to determine Groovebook availability.

use_cases.title: Plan and review feature work
use_cases.description: Turn a feature request into the correct planning, execution, review, or documentation workflow.

use_cases.title: Navigate team workflows
use_cases.description: Find task, memory, and session commands without memorizing the complete Groove catalog.

use_cases.title: Manage Groove installations
use_cases.description: Reach configuration, update, hook, and health-check workflows with confirmation before sensitive changes.

prompt_templates.title: Explore available workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the Groove command catalog.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you are new to Groove or do not know which workflow applies.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the authentication flow for passwordless login and include migration constraints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you have a defined outcome and need an implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Review an implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current branch against the authentication plan and identify required rework.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after implementation to evaluate the result against its intended outcome.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a complex change
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this branch for blind spots across data migration, rollback, tests, and operational readiness.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a broad engineering audit that needs explicit risk coverage.

output_examples.input: Show me the available Groove commands.
output_examples.output: The skill displays grouped Daily, Work, Task, Memory, Session, and Admin commands.

output_examples.input: Plan the authentication flow for passwordless login.
output_examples.output: Routing to Groove Work Plan with the authentication flow details preserved.

output_examples.input: Update Groove to the latest version.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for confirmation before routing to the Groove administration update workflow.

best_practices: State one desired outcome and include the relevant component or scope.
Answer clarification questions when several Groove workflows could satisfy the request.
Review confirmation prompts carefully before administration or publishing workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated workflows in one routing request.
Do not request Groovebook actions when Groovebook is not configured.
Do not bypass confirmation for installation, update, configuration, or publishing actions.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It maps a natural-language request to one matching Groove workflow skill.

faq.question: Can it show every available command?
faq.answer: Yes. Submit no request, or ask for the catalog, to view grouped commands.

faq.question: What happens when a request is ambiguous?
faq.answer: It presents two to four likely workflows and asks you to choose.

faq.question: Does it run administrative actions automatically?
faq.answer: It asks for confirmation before installation, update, configuration, and external publishing workflows.

faq.question: Does it support Groovebook workflows?
faq.answer: Yes, but only when Groovebook is configured in the project Groove settings.

faq.question: Does this skill replace other Groove skills?
faq.answer: No. It routes requests to installed Groove skills that perform the actual work.
